label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7), ramping up over the final original tokens
explanation: Fires almost only at the <DEL> step (about 90% of activation mass), and only when the sequence is long: rate at <DEL> is about 0 for L<=5, low for L=6, high for L=7 and about 100% for L=9. In long sequences it starts ramping up weakly one or two original tokens before <DEL> (mostly the last original token at absolute step t=8 when L=9). Magnitude grows with the absolute step / sequence length and peaks at the <DEL> step of L=8-9 sequences. Token identity hardly matters (all lifts are under 2x). It never fires in the copy phase or at steps t<=4. Misses are mostly weak activations at <DEL> for L=6 and weak pre-<DEL> activity at t=6-7. False positives are L=7-8 <DEL> steps and L=9 final original tokens that fall just under threshold.

issues: The claim 'token identity hardly matters (all lifts under 2x)' is false where the unit is near threshold. The first original token strongly changes the firing rate. At the <DEL> step of L=6 sequences the dev rate is 0.74 for first_tok 't', 0.59 'g', 0.51 'p', 0.46 'j', 0.42 'o', but 0.012 'd', 0.011 'h' and 0.05 'v'. At t=8 (original phase) it is 0.82 for 't' and 0.79 'p' versus 0.17 'h', 0.20 'd' and 0.27 'v'. At t=7 it is 0.44 't' versus 0.02 'd'/'h'. The pooled profile already shows a 2.7x next_out lift for 't', and the pooled tables hide this because L>=7 <DEL> is saturated.

The same first-token ordering (t, p, g, j, o, z, r high; d, h, v, l, x low) shows up in every borderline cell. So the unit's drive is roughly absolute step plus sequence length plus a bias from the first token. The listed misses (weak L=6 <DEL> steps) and false positives (t=8 steps under threshold) are largely this one systematic class, not noise.

Minor: the pre-<DEL> ramp depends on absolute step t, not on position relative to the end of the sequence. Rate at t=7 is 0.137 for L=8 (last token) and 0.142 for L=9 (not last), so 'ramping up over the final original tokens' slightly misdescribes it.

Confirmed claims: about 90% of activation mass is at <DEL>. <DEL> rate is 0.003 at L=5, 0.23 at L=6, 0.86 at L=7, 0.99 at L=8 and 1.00 at L=9. The unit never fires in the copy phase or at t<=4. Rate at t=8 is 0.52. Test F1 0.853 is reproduced.
